_note: Verbatim copy for each prompt WAV. Keys must match src/brain/audio-map.js. Keep the automated-call identification in `greeting`, `ans-bot` and `voicemail-message`. Written for the ear: contractions, short sentences, fragments. Long turns are split so the caller can jump in and so barge-in can resume mid-thought.
greeting: Hi, this is Alex — I'm an automated assistant calling from Softech Innovative Solutions. We build websites and business software. Quick question and then I'll get out of your way: roughly how old is your current website?
pitch-1: Here's why I ask. Most business sites more than about three years old are slow on phones, and awkward to update.
pitch-2: So they quietly leak enquiries. People bounce before the page finishes loading — and you never see those. They just don't call.
pitch-3: We build fast, mobile-first sites, and custom software when a business outgrows the off-the-shelf tools. For most clients it pays for itself in recovered work.
pitch-dated: Right — so that predates the shift where most local searching moved onto phones. That's usually exactly where the leak is.
pitch-nosite: Then this is an easy conversation. Right now every enquiry has to find you some other way — and most people check online before they pick up the phone. We build a simple, fast site: your services, your work, your number. It usually pays for itself pretty quickly.
pitch-followup: So — worth a short chat with one of our consultants, just to see what it'd actually take?
ask-decision-maker: Just so I point you the right way — are you the one who'd make the call on the website and software side?
transfer: Great — let me put you through to one of our senior consultants now. One moment.
close-qualified: Perfect. I'll have one of our consultants get in touch with you directly — they'll walk you through what it would take, and what it would cost, with no obligation either way. Thanks very much for your time, and have a great day.
reprompt: Sorry, I didn't catch that — are you still there?
voicemail-message: Hi, this is Alex, an automated assistant from Softech Innovative Solutions. We build modern websites and business software, and I wanted to see whether there's a fit. Give us a call back any time. Thanks, and have a good day.
reb-ni-1: That's fair, you don't know me yet. Can I give you one sentence? If it's not for you, I'll let you go.
reb-ni-2: Most people say that before they've seen the number. On a dated site, over half of phone visitors leave before it finishes loading. Those are enquiries you never hear about. Want me to check yours? Costs nothing.
reb-ni-3: No problem. Last thing — I'll send a one-page report on your site. Free, and no follow-up unless you ask for it. Fair enough?
reb-has-1: That's good — a lot of our work starts that way. We usually come in on what a single developer doesn't cover: speed, mobile, and where the enquiries actually land. Would a free second opinion help?
reb-has-2: Can I ask — when did they last touch it, and does it load in under three seconds on a phone? If yes, honestly, you're in good shape and I'll leave you alone.
reb-has-3: Understood. I'll send over our audit checklist so you can hold them to it. No cost. Sound good?
reb-hap-1: Good to hear. Out of curiosity — was that a redesign, or a rebuild? A lot of new-looking sites are fresh paint on old plumbing.
reb-hap-2: Fair enough. The two things that catch most people are phone load speed, and whether enquiries reach an inbox somebody actually reads. If both are solid, you're ahead of most.
reb-hap-3: Then you probably don't need me. I'll send our two-minute checklist anyway — worth a glance. Have a good day.
reb-budget-1: Completely understand — and I haven't quoted you anything yet. We phase the work so it fits a budget instead of blowing one, and the first consultation is free.
reb-budget-2: Most of our clients start with the one page that actually brings enquiries, rather than a full rebuild. That's usually a few hundred, not a few thousand.
reb-budget-3: Right, timing's off then. Can I check back after your next budget cycle? No pressure either way.
reb-small-1: That's actually who we do our best work for. Word of mouth still ends with someone looking you up — and if what they find looks dated, you lose them before they ever call. Worth two minutes?
reb-small-2: Fair enough. Even a single fast page with your services and your number on it usually pays for itself. Want me to send an example?
reb-time-1: No problem, I'll be thirty seconds. If it's not relevant you'll know straight away.
reb-think-1: Of course. What's the best email for you? And so it's actually useful — is the concern the cost, the timing, or whether it'd genuinely bring in work?
ans-bot: Yes — I'm an automated assistant from Softech Innovative Solutions. If this sounds like a fit, a human consultant takes over from here. Shall I carry on?
ans-who: This is Alex, calling for Softech Innovative Solutions. We build modern websites, custom software, and mobile apps for businesses.
ans-how: Of course. We found your business through a public listing. It's a short call — and if it's useful, I'll put you straight through to a human consultant.
ans-email: Happy to. I can have a consultant email the details over — or if you've got two minutes now, I'll put you straight through. Which works better?
ans-price: Depends on the scope, and I won't invent a number. A refresh usually starts in the low hundreds; a full custom build is more. A consultant can give you a real figure in a couple of minutes — shall I put you through?
ans-proof: Completely fair to ask. We're Softech Innovative Solutions — you can look us up at ask for it dot I O. I'm an automated assistant, and if this is useful a human takes it from here. Nothing gets sold on this call.
close-not-interested: No problem at all. Thanks for your time — and if things change, we're easy to find. Have a good day.
close-callback: No problem, I'll let you go. We'll try again another time. Have a good day.
close-dnc: Understood — I'll take you off our list right away. Sorry to have bothered you. Goodbye.
close-language: I'm sorry, I don't think I can help in this language. Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
ndm-close: No worries at all — thanks for your time. Have a good day.
close-generic: Thanks for your time. Have a good day.
